key_insight: Combining chest X-rays with basic clinical variables improved AI-based osteoporosis screening, with late-fusion EfficientNetB3 performing best overall.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help identify patients at higher osteoporosis risk using existing chest radiographs when DXA access is limited.
method: Retrospective study of 406 patients aged 50+ with chest X-rays linked to DXA results.
Compared ResNet50 and EfficientNetB3 in image-only, early-fusion, and late-fusion settings.
Used CLAHE + gamma correction, ROI extraction, augmentation, and Optuna-tuned models with a residual MLP for late fusion.
evidence_signal: Late-Fusion EfficientNetB3 achieved the top global chest X-ray result, with AUC 72.73%, and performed consistently better than ResNet50 across local ROI analyses.
watch_item: The dataset was small and imbalanced, so performance may not generalize without external validation and prospective testing.
paper_title: COMBINING CHEST X-RAY AND CLINICAL COVARIATES FOR OSTEOPOROSIS SCREENING: A MULTIMODAL DEEP LEARNING APPROACH
